assessments.rationale: The actual passage explicitly states word-for-word that Cedar Retail refunded duplicate subscription charges.
The passage explicitly states that checkout stayed available during the incident, directly contradicting the claim that it was unavailable.

The passage mentions a specific incident involving a retail company refunding duplicate subscription charges and affecting billing, but it does not define subscription billing or state that it processes payments for recurring retail services.
The passage confirms that Cedar Retail refunded duplicate subscription charges, but it does not specify whether every affected customer was refunded or if the refunds occurred within an hour.
The passage explicitly states that Harbour Parcel paused collections in the coastal district because of flooded roads.
The passage explicitly states that inland collections continued normally, directly opposing the claim that they were suspended.
While the passage mentions a parcel carrier performing collections, it does not specify what is being collected or whether the collections are from retail warehouses.

The passage confirms that collections were paused in the coastal district due to flooded roads, providing context for 'the coastal pause,' but it makes no mention of any retailer or impacts on revenue.
The passage explicitly states that Aster Stores found a stock-counting error and its inventory team corrected the count, which directly supports the claim.
The passage explicitly states that 'no physical goods were lost' in the warehouse stock-counting error, directly contradicting the claim that Aster Stores lost physical goods.

The passage describes a specific incident where a warehouse stock-counting error was corrected, providing related context, but does not state the general rule that inventory records help retailers manage warehouse stock.
The passage explicitly states that the stock-counting error was found in "one warehouse," whereas the claim asserts it affected "all Aster warehouses."
The passage directly states that Linden Payments disabled an experimental payment option after repeated timeouts.
The source explicitly states that card payments remained operational throughout, directly contradicting the claim that card payments stopped working.

The passage mentions a specific company disabling a payment option and keeping card payments operational, which does not establish the broad claim that payment providers process transactions for online merchants.
The passage confirms that the experimental payment option experienced repeated timeouts, but it does not state what caused them or make any mention of a database failure.
The passage explicitly states that Elm Advertising rejected a new creative for violating its image policy, which directly supports the claim.
The passage explicitly states that existing approved campaigns continued to serve, which directly contradicts the claim that all approved campaigns stopped serving.

The passage demonstrates an advertising platform (Elm Advertising) rejecting a new creative for violating an image policy and notes that existing campaigns are 'approved', supporting the claim that creatives are reviewed against policies.
The passage confirms that a creative was rejected, but it does not mention any merchant's sales or any causal effect on sales.
The passage explicitly states that Rowan Market removed a batch of duplicate reviews.
The source explicitly states that Rowan Market retained all verified original reviews, including negative ones, which directly contradicts the claim that they removed all negative verified reviews.
The passage mentions the removal of duplicate reviews and retention of verified reviews at Rowan Market, but it does not state what customer reviews describe or mention shopping experiences.
The passage mentions that duplicate reviews were removed, but it provides no information about who created them or whether a competitor was involved.
The passage directly states that Birch Outfitters extended its returns window for winter purchases.
The source explicitly states that summer purchases kept the existing returns policy, and only the returns window for winter purchases was extended.

The passage mentions a company's returns window and returns policy for seasonal purchases, providing related context, but does not define what returns policies are or state that they explain how customers can return purchases.
The passage mentions a change to the returns window for winter purchases, but it provides no information on whether this change affected customer retention.
The passage explicitly states verbatim that Juniper Commerce completed scheduled catalogue maintenance.
The passage explicitly states that the payment service was not part of the maintenance, directly contradicting the claim that it was included.

The passage mentions catalogue maintenance and product browsing resuming, which provides related context, but it does not explicitly state the general definition that online catalogues let customers browse products.
The passage confirms that scheduled catalogue maintenance was completed, but it provides no information regarding the duration of the maintenance.
The actual passage explicitly states that Maple Delivery rerouted northern shipments around a closed bridge, matching the proposed claim verbatim.
The passage explicitly states that northern shipments were rerouted around the closed bridge, while southern shipments followed their usual routes, directly contradicting the claim.
The passage mentions delivery shipments and routes, but it does not state whether delivery routes connect warehouses and destinations.
The passage states that northern shipments were rerouted, but it does not mention whether they arrived late or on time.
The passage directly states that Willow Shop withdrew an expired promotion code.
The passage directly contradicts the claim by stating that Willow Shop's active promotion codes remained valid and usable at checkout, whereas the claim states they could not be used.
The passage confirms that promotion codes are usable at checkout, but does not explicitly state that they apply discounts.
The passage confirms that an expired promotion code was withdrawn while active codes remained valid, but it mentions nothing about conversion rates or any impact caused by the expired code.
The passage explicitly states that Quartz Fulfilment reported delays for refrigerated orders.

The passage explicitly states that standard orders met their promised delivery dates and that delays were reported for refrigerated orders only, directly contradicting the claim that standard orders missed their delivery dates.
The passage mentions delays for refrigerated orders at Quartz Fulfilment, but it does not define refrigerated fulfilment or state that it transports temperature-sensitive products.

The passage confirms that Quartz Fulfilment had delays for refrigerated orders, but explicitly notes that the report did not estimate lost revenue, providing no evidence that the delays caused a revenue decline.
The passage explicitly states that Opal Commerce observed a traffic increase during a public festival, which directly supports the claim without claiming causation.
The passage explicitly states that analysts did not establish what caused the traffic increase, which directly contradicts the claim that they established the festival caused it.
The passage mentions a traffic increase observed by Opal Commerce and analysts, but it does not specifically mention website analytics, online stores, or how visits are recorded.

The passage notes that a traffic increase occurred during the festival, but explicitly states that observations did not establish what caused the increase, providing insufficient evidence to support a causal claim.
The passage explicitly notes that Amber Checkout published a report stating that service recovered on Monday evening.

The passage states that Amber Checkout reported on Tuesday that the service interruption from Monday had already recovered on Monday evening, contradicting the claim that service remained interrupted throughout Tuesday.

The passage explicitly mentions a published report about a service interruption and its subsequent recovery, which directly supports the claim that service status reports describe availability incidents.
The passage confirms a service interruption occurred on Monday and recovered that evening, but it does not state when the interruption began.
The passage explicitly states that Coral Ads restored reporting for search campaigns.
The passage states that Coral Ads' notice said display reporting was still delayed, whereas only reporting for search campaigns was restored.
The passage mentions search and display campaign reporting status for Coral Ads, but it does not define what advertising reports are or state that they summarise campaign measurements.
The passage only mentions reporting issues for search and display campaigns and explicitly notes that the notice did not discuss campaign delivery.
The passage only states that Indigo Retail claimed ('Indigo said') its inspection found no defect, which is insufficient to verify as an objective fact that the inspection actually found no defect.
The source passage directly contradicts the claim, stating that Indigo Retail's inspection found no defect in the inspected batch.
The passage mentions a packaging defect allegation and an inspection of a batch, but it does not state when packaging inspections occur or whether they check products before shipment.

The passage states that only one inspected batch was found to have no defect according to Indigo Retail, while other batches had not been inspected. It does not support the claim that every batch was free of defects.
The passage explicitly states that Topaz Market confirmed that its warehouse reopened after an inspection.
The passage explicitly states that Topaz Market denied any stock loss, directly contradicting the claim that it confirmed stock was lost.

The passage mentions a specific warehouse reopening after an inspection, which provides topical context, but it does not state a general definition that warehouse inspections assess storage facilities.
The passage confirms that Topaz Market's warehouse reopened after an inspection, but it makes no mention of sales or whether the reopening increased them.
